key_insight: A large bilingual radiology dataset can train a single vision-language model to generate reports, answer questions, and localize findings without manual spatial labels.
clinical_relevance: This could support radiology workflows by improving open-ended image understanding while also making outputs spatially checkable for safer review.
method: Built RefRad2D from 1.2M CT/MR image-text pairs in German and English.
Automatically created VQA and grounding subsets using LLM-based curation and segmentation tools.
Trained RadGrounder to jointly do report generation, VQA, and bounding-box or segmentation-based grounding.
evidence_signal: On external VQA benchmarks (Slake and VQA-RAD), the model was competitive with specialized medical VLMs, and adding clinical pretraining data improved open-ended VQA without hurting language quality.
watch_item: The grounding subsets were generated automatically, so label noise and dataset bias could affect real-world reliability and require careful validation.
paper_title: Scalable Training of Spatially Grounded 2D Vision-Language Models for Radiology
